name: New Mexico
scope: Statewide Alimony Guidelines and Commentaries (revised September 6, 2006), published on nmcourts.gov; advisory, used with the factors of NMSA 1978 § 40-4-7(E).
formulaText: Alimony Guideline Worksheet: no children for whom support is paid: 30% of payor's gross monthly income minus 50% of recipient's gross monthly income; with children for whom support is paid: 28% of payor's gross monthly income minus 58% of recipient's. Zero or negative = no alimony. Gross income = child support definition (NMSA 1978 § 40-4-11.1). Alimony is computed first and then subtracted from / added to gross incomes for child support. No cap recommended, but in high-income cases the guideline may be unreasonable.
durationText: Commentary II.F: 0 to < 5 years of marriage: generally no alimony; 5 to < 10: generally only rehabilitative or transitional; > 10 to < 20: some states use 30% to 50% of the years of marriage; > 20 years: the court reserves jurisdiction unless the parties agree to lump-sum non-modifiable support.
eligibilityText: NMSA 1978 § 40-4-7(E) factors (age and health, earnings and earning capacity, good-faith efforts to be self-supporting, reasonable needs, duration of marriage, property awarded, assets, liabilities, income from property, agreements), reproduced in the guidelines.

durationTable.rule: durational range used by some states (illustrative)

facts.text: New Mexico's guideline formula was modelled on the Fairfax County, Virginia pendente lite guideline.
The guideline sets no income cap, consistent with New Mexico's child support guidelines.

sources.name: IRS Topic no. 452, Alimony and separate maintenance
